communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Salem Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

Also note that after a thorough review of our files, the Salem Police Department's Records Office has identified an email responsive to your request. However, we are unable to release this record, as it is legally exempt from mandatory public disclosure.
Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law<https://www.mass.gov/files/2017-06/Public%20Records%20Law.pdf>, G.L. c. 4, § 7(26)<https://www.mass.gov/info-details/exemptions>, the requested email is being withheld in its entirety under the following legal protections:
Basis for Exemption

  *
Common Law Attorney-Client Privilege: Under established Massachusetts common law, confidential communications between a governmental entity and its legal counsel are strictly protected from disclosure to ensure the public entity can obtain candid, reliable legal advice. See Suffolk Construction Co. v. Division of Capital Asset Management, 449 Mass. 444 (2007). The withheld email (dated 8-24-26) is that of the Chief of Police Lucas Miller. It is a confidential communication sent to Eric Atstupenas, the General Counsel for the Massachusetts Chiefs of Police Association seeking specific legal advisement on policy and protocol interpretations regarding Protect Act compliance.

Exemption (d) — Deliberative Process / Policy Development: Pursuant to G.L. c. 4, § 7(26)(d)<https://www.mass.gov/guide-to-evidence/section-518-executive-or-governmental-privilege>, public records do not include intra-agency or inter-agency memos or letters relating to policy positions currently being developed. This email consists of pre-decisional protocol and policy questions aimed at establishing compliance frameworks. Release of this preliminary, deliberative information would stifle the free, honest exchange of ideas required for law enforcement agencies to successfully navigate new regulatory requirements.

Due to the fact that the entire substance of the communication consists of a request for legal consultation and ongoing policy formulation, there are no segregable, purely factual portions that can be redacted and released.
No additional responsive records were located in the custody or control of this office.

Please be advised that pursuant to 950 CMR 32.00 and G.L. c. 66, § 10A(a), you have the right to appeal this decision to the Supervisor of Public Records within 90 calendar days. Such appeal must be in writing and should include a copy of your original request and, if available, this response. Please note that the Supervisor may only consider appeals arising from written public records requests. Pursuant to G.L. c. 66, § 10A(c), you also have the right to seek judicial review by commencing a civil action in Superior Court.

title: How Michigan approves and tests tax software: Treasury's records on Intuit's Michigan products, e-file Business Rule 74, and notices to software developers about the Earned Income Tax Credit for part-year residents (2013 to present)

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: How Michigan approves and tests tax software: Treasury's records on Intuit's Michigan products, e-file Business Rule 74, and notices to software developers about the Earned Income Tax Credit for part-year resid
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

In one sentence: this request asks how the Department of Treasury approves and tests tax preparation software for Michigan returns, what its e-file Business Rule 74 has said since 2013, and what it told software developers before and after Intuit Inc. corrected its Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit calculation for part-year residents in 2024.

Context, from public sources. Intuit stated on its ProSeries community board on April 23, 2024 that the Michigan EITC calculation was incorrect for part-year resident filers in its tax year 2022 and 2023 Michigan programs, with corrections released March 7, 2024 and April 18, 2024, and its TurboTax support site states that "Some Michigan TurboTax customers have overpaid their state taxes due to an error with the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit." Treasury records released under FOIA on July 28 and August 11, 2026 show that Treasury's e-file Business Rule 74 was based on an April 2, 2012 Treasury memorandum and that its logic had not been updated since tax year 2013. Treasury's software developer page states that every developer producing Michigan tax preparation software must complete Form 4430, the Michigan Letter of Intent to Participate in E-File and Substitute Forms Programs.

Definitions. "Intuit" means Intuit Inc., its subsidiaries, employees, agents and counsel, including any address at intuit.com. "Intuit's Michigan products" means TurboTax, ProSeries, ProConnect and Lacerte as used to prepare Michigan individual income tax returns. "Communications" includes email with attachments, letters, memoranda, bulletins, and messages in any ticketing or case system.

Records requested, in order of priority:

1. Approval and testing of Intuit's Michigan products, tax years 2021 through 2025. Form 4430 submissions by Intuit; Treasury's approval, acceptance, rejection or conditional-approval communications for Intuit's Michigan individual income tax products; test package results, and any test scenario, for returns of part-year residents claiming the Michigan EITC; any notice of error, defect or correction that Intuit submitted to Treasury; and any suspension, revocation or corrective-action correspondence. Where a record contains confidential commercial information, please release the nonexempt portions under MCL 15.244.

2. Business Rule 74. The text of Business Rule 74 as published to software developers for each of tax years 2013 through 2025; any change log or version history; and the records of the March 2024 internal review in which Individual Income Tax management concurred that the rule's logic remained applicable, including the two messages released on August 11, 2026 and anything beyond them.

3. Notices to all software developers. Bulletins, memoranda, test-package changes, or messages to the software developer distribution list concerning Michigan EITC eligibility or computation for part-year or nonresident filers, from January 1, 2022 through the date of your search, including anything issued after March 7, 2024. Documents currently posted on Treasury's public software developer site may be excluded if you identify each excluded document by title and date.

4. All-vendor counts. Any existing aggregate record of Business Rule 74 rejection counts for all software vendors, or for vendors other than Intuit, by processing year, without identifiers, product names or taxpayer-specific facts. I am not asking Treasury to create a record; if no such existing record is retained, please state that in the response.

5. Who else has asked. The entries in Treasury's FOIA request log or tracking system for requests received from January 1, 2024 through the date of your search that concern Intuit, TurboTax, ProSeries or the Michigan EITC, with requesters' personal information redacted.

Records released previously. The April 2, 2012 memorandum "MI EITC and nonresidents" and the "EIC Question" messages of March 6 and 7, 2024 were released under FOIA on July 28 and August 11, 2026. Please include them again in response to item 2, so that the public record on this page is complete.

Custodians and search terms. Forms, Documentation and E-file Services, including MIFormsEfile@michigan.gov and the staff who administer the software developer program; the Tax Processing Bureau; Individual Income Tax Division management; the FOIA Coordinator's office; and Heather Vellanti and Scott Bunnells, whom Treasury's released records identify. Suggested search terms: Intuit, TurboTax, ProSeries, ProConnect, Lacerte, "Form 4430", "letter of intent", "test package", ATS, EITC, EIC, "earned income", "part-year", nonresident, "Business Rule 74", BR74.

Format. Under MCL 15.234(1)(c), please provide the records electronically, as native email files (.eml or .msg) with attachments where they exist, otherwise as searchable PDF.

Fees. I ask that Treasury waive or reduce fees under MCL 15.234(2). The records concern how the state approves the software that prepares most Michigan returns and how a publicly acknowledged calculation error in a credit for working families with low incomes passed through that process, and every record released will be published without charge on this public page for anyone to read. I am an individual requester and the request has no commercial purpose. If a fee is charged, please send the detailed itemization required by MCL 15.234(4) before processing. If the estimate exceeds $300, please contact me before doing any work so that I can narrow the request, and in any case please process the items in the order listed. Any deposit is limited to half of the estimate under MCL 15.234(8).

If any part is denied, please cite the specific exemption for each record or portion, release the nonexempt portions under MCL 15.244, and describe what is withheld. Please respond within the 5 business days provided by MCL 15.235(2).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Burak Genc

Burak,

This written notice is issued in response to your October 14, 2026, email (below) received by the Michigan Department of Treasury (Treasury) on October 15, 2026, requesting records under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), MCL 15.231 et seq. As set forth in Treasury's October 22, 2026, response, a statutory extension of time to respond was taken.

In your request, you asked for:

"1. Approval and testing of Intuit's Michigan products, tax years 2021 through 2025. Form 4430 submissions by Intuit; Treasury's approval, acceptance, rejection or conditional-approval communications for Intuit's Michigan individual income tax products; test package results, and any test scenario, for returns of part-year residents claiming the Michigan EITC; any notice of error, defect or correction that Intuit submitted to Treasury; and any suspension, revocation or corrective-action correspondence. 3. Notices to all software developers. 4. All-vendor counts. 5. Who else has asked. The entries in Treasury's FOIA request log or tracking system for requests received from January 1, 2024 through the date of your search that concern Intuit, TurboTax, ProSeries or the Michigan EITC, with requesters' personal information redacted.

Records released previously. The April 2, 2012 memorandum "MI EITC and nonresidents" and the "EIC Question" messages of March 6 and 7, 2024 were released under FOIA on July 28 and August 11, 2026. Your request is granted in part and denied in part.

Items 1-4: To the extent responsive records exist, they are exempt from disclosure pursuant to section 13(1)(d) of the FOIA, MCL 15.243(1)(d), which exempts from disclosure records or information specifically described and exempted from disclosure under another statute. Section 28(1)(f) of the Revenue Act, MCL 205.28(1)(f), prohibits the disclosure of any facts or information obtained in connection with the administration of a tax, or information or parameters that would enable a person to ascertain the audit selection or processing criteria of the Department, for taxes administered by the Department.

Accordingly, individuals' name(s) and email address(es) have been redacted.

Box 30716, Lansing, MI 48909. The writing must specifically state the word "appeal" and must identify the reason or reasons the requester believes the partial denial should be reversed. communications.communication:
Hi Andrea,

Checking in on those audit logs again. If no progress has been made on generating an audit log, please provide an explanation as to why that is.

DPD/DOS Records previously provided audit logs to the public during the tenure of the Flock Safety ALPR program. I've looked through Axon's user guides for generating audit logs and it is very clearly a built-in functionality, core to the product that DPD's RTCC should have access to.

Furthermore, DPD's OM explicitly calls out the ability for audits to be conducted. Per DPD's OM:
"119.03 AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE READER SYSTEM

(5) ALPRS, AUDITING, AND OVERSIGHT:

d.      A list of all officers who are authorized to have access to the system will be maintained by the RTCC. RTCC will also ensure:
1. A log is maintained when access to ALPR images and data is requested, whether internal or external and will include the date, time, data record accessed, officer or officers involved, case number and purpose of the request.
2. The log will be provided for internal and external audits and internal investigations.
3. Regular oversight over use of the system, including periodic, random audits to ensure and evaluate compliance with policy and applicable law and appropriate purging and storage or data and images pursuant to this policy and Colorado law. A supervisor in the TESU unit will be responsible for conducting periodic audits."

Please provide the maintained log with all the details listed in the Operations Manual, or an explanation of why the records are not maintained by DPD as the policy dictates.

Thank you,
William Beckett

communications.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] Colorado Open Records Act Request: DPD Search logs/audit logs from Axon ALPR System (Denver Police Department)
communications.communication:
Good afternoon Mr. Beckett –
Following a good faith search, please see the attached records responsive to your request available to the public. Records of the Denver Police Department are criminal justice records, the disclosure of which is governed by the Colorado Criminal Justice Records Act (CCJRA), sections 24-72-301, et. seq. C.R.S.  Except for records of “official actions,” the disclosure of criminal justice records is discretionary and can be denied where the custodian believes disclosure would be contrary to the public interest. Section 24-72-305(5), C.R.S.
 Pursuant to Harris v. Denver Post, 123 P.3d 116 (Colo. 2005), the following factors , in addition to other relevant considerations,  may be used to determine whether a record should be released or withheld:

  1.  the privacy interests of individuals, if any, who may be impacted by a decision to allow disclosure of the record;
  2.  the agency’s interest in keeping confidential information confidential;
  3.  the agency’s interest in the integrity of on-going investigations;
  4.  the public purpose to be served in allowing disclosure of the record; and
  5.  any other pertinent considerations relevant to the circumstances of the records request, including whether disclosure would be contrary to the public interest.
Based upon my consideration of the relevant factors, I have determined that certain information should be redacted from the report prior to public disclosure to protect privacy and interests which outweigh the public interest in disclosure of the information.  The redacted columns include, names of officers, case numbers, time frame, license plate information, search coordinates, vehicle description, filters (which included case numbers and other information related to criminal investigation)s) and entries from within the reason column have been redacted.
We also want to proactively share some important context with you regarding two entries in the May audit log.

The two queries on May 19, 2026, with the offense category listed as “Other; Immigration Violator” were test queries submitted by Denver Police personnel during DPD’s testing phase conducted prior to the go-live date of June 3, 2026, for its Axon ALPR pilot program. More specifically, the queries were submitted to see if the system would allow such a query and how it would be reported in the audit so that DPD could provide feedback to the vendor. So, to be clear, these two queries were submitted for the purpose of testing the system prior to implementation and were not submitted for the purpose of any enforcement.
In accordance with Denver municipal ordinance and Colorado law, the Denver Police Department does not assist with the enforcement of civil federal immigration laws.

Thank you,

Andrea

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Shrewsbury Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: Minneapolis and St. Paul Police - LexisNexis / AVCC Data Sharing (Minneapolis Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

REQUEST: Please provide all emails between employees of your police department and LexisNexis from October 1, 2025 through July 28, 2026. You may de-duplicate emails if the same email was sent to multiple employees. Please include attachments. Please ensure the responsive emails and documents are preserved during the time it takes to process this request. The LexisNexis email domains are @LexisNexisRisk.com and @LexisNexis.com 

CONTEXT: During Operation Metro Surge, LexisNexis wrote an email stating that they hope to soon have data from Minneapolis Police and St. Paul Police available to subscribers of Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC). LexisNexis has AVCC contracts with, and sells data access to ICE, the Navy, the VA, the DOJ, and 2,400 federal and local agencies around the U.S., meaning they can view victim and witness details of police reports and 911 calls from departments that allow LexisNexis to copy their data. We are trying to understand whether your agency has started sharing your CAD/RMS data with federal agencies via LexisNexis's AVCC / Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.communication:
Hi Elizabeth, thank you very much for sending this info. I have two quick questions. For the first email in the responsive PDF you sent, there's no date in the header. Are you able to tell me when MPD received that email? Part of what we're attempting to determine is when access was originally set up with LexisNexis. 

The second image I attached here includes a reference to some slides or flyers being shared, but there were no attachments included. Are those attachments being withheld, were they outside the scope of my request, or should they have been included? Thanks for taking a look at both those things, I appreciate it!

Best,
Shawn

title: UFC event (Washington State Fusion Center)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: UFC event (Washington State Fusion Center)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All Advisories, Suspicious Activity Reports, Tips, Intelligence Briefs, Intel Reports, Leads Information or Data, Maps, Bulletins, BOLOs, and/or Joint Bulletins from July 3, 2025 to June 16, 2026 (inclusive) regarding the planned Ultimate Fighting Championship event at the White House, known as "UFC Freedom 250" or "UFC at the White House."

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

title: BPD Basic Data Request 11/2020

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: BPD Basic Data Request 11/2020
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

11/1/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of the following fields of information for all Boston Police Department employees from 11/1/2020 to 12/1/2020. Please include the following fields of information:
 
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (475)-243-3786 and mchristi@bu.edu

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

Sincerely,
Michael Christie
BU SPARK!

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

communications.subject: Florida Sunshine Law Request: flock clone (City Of Oviedo)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Florida Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

Under Article I, section 24 of the Florida Constitution and Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, I request copies of public records concerning the investigation and arrest involving an alleged decoy or replica Flock Safety camera reported by ClickOrlando on August 23, 2026.
News report: https://www.clickorlando.com/news/local/2026/08/23/oviedo-arrest-over-decoy-flock-camera-raises-questions-about-surveillance/

Please provide the following records:
- All incident, offense, arrest, supplemental, investigative, and probable-cause reports concerning the decoy or replica camera and the related arrest.

- All arrest warrants, search warrants, warrant applications, affidavits, returns, inventories, subpoenas, court orders, consent-to-search forms, and preservation requests associated with the investigation.

- All photographs, videos, body-worn-camera recordings, dashboard-camera recordings, surveillance footage, drone footage, diagrams, measurements, maps, sketches, and scene documentation depicting the device, its installation, its location, or its removal.

- All records concerning the design, creation, fabrication, assembly, installation, operation, intended use, or testing of the alleged decoy camera that were obtained, collected, copied, downloaded, submitted, or created during the investigation.

This specifically includes, without limitation:
Native 3D-printing and design files, including STL, 3MF, OBJ, AMF, STEP, STP, IGES, CAD, OpenSCAD, Blender, Fusion 360, SolidWorks, Cura, PrusaSlicer, G-code, project, and slicer-profile files;

Drawings, schematics, dimensions, measurements, templates, parts lists, bills of materials, assembly instructions, build notes, revisions, prototypes, and design histories;

Source images, photographs, scans, photogrammetry files, reference models, and specifications used to reproduce the appearance of a Flock Safety camera;

Files or instructions obtained from websites, cloud services, social-media accounts, messaging platforms, removable media, computers, phones, or other digital devices; and

Any investigative copies, forensic images, exports, screenshots, printouts, or derivative versions of these materials.

All communications concerning this incident between or among the Oviedo Police Department and:

Flock Safety or its representatives;

The City of Oviedo;

The Seminole County Sheriff’s Office;

The State Attorney’s Office;

Other law-enforcement agencies;

Property owners, homeowners’ associations, utilities, or contractors; and

Members of the public, witnesses, complainants, or news organizations.

This includes emails, attachments, text messages, messaging-app communications, memoranda, letters, call logs, meeting notes, and communications sent through personal accounts or devices when used for official business.

Any press releases, media talking points, public statements, internal summaries, briefing materials, or records prepared in response to media inquiries regarding this incident.

Requested format

Please provide records electronically by email or downloadable link. For electronic records—particularly design, CAD, 3D-printing, source-code, configuration, and metadata-bearing files—I request the native electronic files in the format in which the agency maintains or received them. Please do not substitute screenshots, paper printouts, or flattened PDF versions when native files exist.

Please preserve associated metadata, original filenames, directory structure, and available creation and modification dates. If forensic software does not permit production in native form, please provide the ordinary export format and any accompanying report that identifies the original filename, path, metadata, and hash value.

Please do not withhold an entire record merely because one portion is exempt. If records are held by another department, employee, contractor, cloud provider, forensic vendor, or agency on the City’s behalf, please include those records or identify the appropriate custodian.

Please acknowledge receipt and provide an estimated production date. If responsive records can be produced on a rolling basis, please provide them as they become available rather than waiting until the entire request is complete.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Jason Koebler

title: Flock Safety Event Log, May 15, 2026 to Present

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Safety Event Log, May 15, 2026 to Present
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting the Flock Safety Event Log for the Savannah Police Department’s Flock account, covering every organization or network in the account, from May 15, 2026, through the date of this request. This is the export of user and administrative actions with the columns Timestamp, User, Event Type, Entity Type, Entity Details, and Event Id. It is not the license plate search audit.

In priority order:

Every event other than live stream views, for example, network share changes (create, update, or delete), custom hotlist entries, recorded stream views, and stream downloads.
The live stream view events.
Any documentation from Flock or kept by the Department that explains the Event Log’s fields, event types, and entity types.

If item 2 is large or costly, please send items 1 and 3 first and give me the estimate for item 2. I am glad to narrow its date range or scope.

Please provide the log as a CSV or the platform’s native export so I can search it. If the platform limits the export size or period, please provide as many exports as needed to cover the whole period with no gaps, and tell me the first and last event date in each file. This includes records Flock Safety maintains for the Department. See O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(a)(2)(B).

If any part cannot be released, please tell me which part and the specific legal authority by Code section, subsection, and paragraph, as § 50-18-71(d) provides, and release the rest. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

communications.subject: RE: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Safety Event Log, May 15, 2026 to Present
communications.communication:
Thank you for the two worksheets. Three things are still missing.

First, user names. The request asked for a User column, but the file gives only a User External ID code. Please provide the Flock user list mapping each External ID to the user’s name, role, and account status, or add the names.

Second, the entity column. Section 35-1-22(f) exempts captured license plate data, which section 35-1-22(a)(2) defines as the coordinates, date and time, photograph, and plate number captured by or derived from the license plate system. Camera and stream names, the organizations a network was shared with, role names, and user-account names are not that data. Please restore the entity column for every row except the Custom Hotlist Entry rows, and for the hotlist rows, blank the plate number and release the rest. That is a column edit and does not need review of individual cells, so I am not asking for the cell-by-cell review described in your message.

Third, if the Department still withholds entity information under § 50-18-72(a)(4), please identify the paragraph and the pending investigation it relates to, as § 50-18-71(d) provides, and release the rest.

Item 3 of my request (documentation explaining the Event Log’s fields, event types, and entity types) was not addressed. Please provide it or tell me in writing that none exists. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

title: Adams 12 Five Star Schools Open Records Request - Student Enrollment Data

communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Adams 12 Five Star Schools Open Records Request - Student Enrollment Data
communications.communication:
Dear Open Records Coordinator,

I am writing on behalf of the Data Acquisition Lab to formally request access to public records under the Colorado Open Records Act § 24-72-201 et seq. We are requesting aggregated counts of student enrollment at the most granular geographic level available, which will enable a more meaningful understanding of community-level trends. We plan to request this information on a bi-annual basis going forward.

I am specifically requesting a tabular dataset containing the counts of enrolled students in Adams 12 Five Star Schools for the current 2025-2026 school year, disaggregated by the following fields:

- School identifier (name, NCES ID)
- Census tract GEOID (full 11-digit or abbreviated 6-digit code), census tract, or de-identified address
- Grade level
- Student enrollment count

Privacy Considerations:
- This request does not seek, nor does it require, personally identifiable information (PII) or any data points that could reasonably be used to identify individual students or households.
- We respect the importance of compliance with all applicable privacy laws. If additional thresholds or adjustments are required to ensure absolute privacy, we are happy to collaborate on refinements to the data as necessary.

If certain records or portions of records are exempt from disclosure, please provide a written explanation of the specific exemption(s) and release any non-exempt portions of the requested records. If this data is not centrally held, please advise which agency holds this data. Thank you for your attention to this request. If you have any questions or require further information, please feel free to contact me.

communications.subject: South Dakota Open Records Law Request: Deaths-in-custody (South Dakota Department of Public Safety)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the South Dakota Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all Illinois law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant both Illinois state legislation (730 ILCS 210/3-5) and federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organizatin of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: USAID Ebola audits
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

- All the drafts or final reports of audits and/or investigations and/or desk reviews undertaken by the Office of the Inspector General on the response to the 10th, 11th and/or 12th Ebola epidemics in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The timeframe is 14 April 2020 to today. This includes any updates regarding complaint 19-0852 and 20-0502 inter alia.
- All reports of the visit  by a delegation of U.S. officials to the Democratic Republic of Congo to assess the response to the outbreak. The timeframe is 14 April 2020 until today-

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emmanuel Freudenthal

communications.subject: FOIA processing delays due to COVID-19 Re: Freedom of Information Act Request: USAID Ebola audits
communications.communication:
USAID has implemented maximum telework to promote social distancing during the COVID-19 pandemic.  Priorities in many of our operating units have shifted, thus impacting processing response times. Please note that USAID is unable to conduct a search for physical records while teleworking.  As a result, all search requests will be limited to electronic records, unless you notify us that you want your request to remain open until USAID employees have physical access to their workspaces. We appreciate your understanding during this time.  If you have any questions, please email us at foia@usaid.gov .  Thank you.

communications.subject: USAID FOIA REQUEST No. F-00026-22 (FOIA Specialist Assignment Email)
communications.communication:
October 21, 2021 RE:  USAID FOIA No. F-00026-22 (FOIA Specialist Assignment Email) Dear Mr. Freudenthal: This acknowledges receipt of your October 21, 2021, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).  Specifically, you requested records concerning: All the drafts or final reports of audits and/or investigations and/or desk reviews undertaken by the Office of the Inspector General on the response to the 10th, 11th and/or 12th Ebola epidemics in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The timeframe is 14 April 2020 to today. This includes any updates regarding complaint 19-0852 and 20-0502 inter alia.- All reports of the visit by a delegation of U.S. officials to the Democratic Republic of Congo to assess the response to the outbreak. The timeframe is 14 April 2020 until today-(Date Range for Record Search: From 4/14/2020 To 10/21/2021). 
Fee 
The FOIA provides that fees should be waived or reduced if disclosure of the information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.  As a member of the media, the only applicable fee is duplication.  Duplication is $0.10 per page, but the first 100 pages are free. Since the only applicable fee is duplication, and USAID routinely furnishes responsive records to FOIA requesters in electronic format, it's most likely there will be no duplication fees to assess. 
FOIA Specialist 
Your request has been assigned to Theresa Morris, Senior FOIA Specialist.  You may contact Theresa Morris by email at thmorris@usaid.gov or by phone on 202-921-5003.  Please reference the tracking number cited above in any future correspondence. 
Extending the FOIA’s Time Limits due to Unusual Circumstances The FOIA provides that an agency  may extend its time limits when “unusual circumstances” occur in the processing of a request. See 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B)(i) (2016).  Those “unusual circumstances” are set forth in the statute, 5 U.S.C § 552(a)(6)(B)(iii), and are described as: 1) The need to search for records from field facilities or other locations separate from the office processing the request; 2) The need to search, collect and examine voluminous records; and 3) The need for consultation with another agency. Based upon the records you have requested, we have determined that one or more unusual circumstances will occur during the processing of your request.  Accordingly, your response time-limit has been extended beyond the 20 days required by statute; therefore, 10 additional processing days have been added to your request. To mitigate this action, you may limit the scope of the request so that it can be processed more quickly or to arrange an alternative time to respond. If you have any questions or wish to discuss reformulation or an alternative time frame for the processing of your request, you may contact the assigned FOIA Specialist noted above. You may also contact USAID’s FOIA Public Liaison, Christopher Colbow, at foia@usaid.gov. (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) 

Additionally, you may contact the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) at the National Archives and Records Administration to inquire about the FOIA mediation services offered: Office of Government Information Services National Archives and Records Administration 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001 E-mail: ogis@nara.gov Telephone: 202-741-5770; Toll Free: 1-877-684-6448 Fax: 202-741-5769 Thank you for your interest in USAID. Sincerely, Diamond Johnson 
FOIA Specialist 
Bureau for Management 
Office of Management Services 
Information and Records Division

communications.subject: USAID FOIA Email Receipt RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #F-00026-22
communications.communication:
Greetings - 

Thank you for contacting the USAID FOIA office. We have received your request and will respond within 48 hours. 

Kindly be informed of the following: 

Requesting records containing personally identifiable information (PII): 
1st Party Request: 
If you are requesting records about yourself, we must verify your identity prior to initiating a search for records. Please complete and return t he AID form 507-1, Certification of Identity, located here: https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1. Please submit the completed form in addition to the source documents outlined in section 2 encrypted via (https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1) foia@usaid.gov, accompanied by a password in a separate email. (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) 
3rd Party Request: 
If you are requesting records concerning another individual on their behalf, you must provide a statement from that individual verifying their identity. Please have the subject of the request complete sections 1 and 2 of the AID form 507-1, Certification of Identity, located here: https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1. As the 3rd party requester, please complete section 3. Send the completed form and source documents outlined in section 2 encrypted via (https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1) foia@usaid.gov, accompanied by a password, prior initiating a search for records. (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) 
Requesting acquisition (contracts, etc.) and assistance (grants, cooperative agreements, etc.) awards: 

We receive many requests for procurement documents: solicitations, proposals, and contracts. Sometimes our requesters only provide us with the solicitation number. If possible, when you are requesting winning proposals, please provide the following additional information: the office that issued the solicitation, the title of the solicitation, the name of the successful bidder, and the number of the resulting award. For procurement documents, please provide the award number, office that issued the award, program name, and geographic location. 

Thank you, 

USAID FOIA Team 

-- 
V/r, FOIA Specialist US AID - US Agency for International Development FOIA Office Bureau for Management, Office of Management Services, Information and Records Division (M/MS/IRD) | foia@USAID.gov

Dear Sir/Maam,

"On September 18, 2025, USAID sent you a letter pursuant to its “Still Interested” notice published in the Federal Register on September 16, 2025. The letter asked you to confirm whether you wished for USAID to continue processing your FOIA request and provided a response deadline of October 31, 2025.

Because we did not receive a response from you by the October 31, 2025, deadline, your FOIA request has been administratively closed under the “Still Interested” notice procedure.

If you wish USAID to reopen your request, you may reply to this email confirming that you remain interested. Please do this within five business days.  Once we have your confirmation, we will reopen and resume processing the request.

If we do not receive a reply, no further action will be taken.

Please feel free to contact us with any questions.

V/r, 
FOIA Specialist
USAID - US Agency for International Development FOIA Office
Bureau for Management, Office of Management Services, Information and Records Division (M/MS/IRD) | foia@USAID.gov"

Derwin"

Best regards,
Emmanuel

title: EMAILS REGARDING BEND POLICE

communications.subject: Oregon Public Records Law Request: EMAILS REGARDING BEND POLICE
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Specifically, I am requesting the following emails generated or received between January 1, 2024, and the date this request is processed: Copies of all formal and informal comments or complaints,  filed by members of the public or city employees regarding the conduct, policies, or actions of the City of Bend Police Department.  Copies of the 96 emails categorized under the "Police" topic sent to the City Council across the 2024, 2025, and 2026 calendar years dashboard.   

I request a full waiver of all fees associated with fulfilling this request. As a representative of the independent news outlet StateCreated.net, I am requesting this information for news-gathering and publication purposes. The disclosure of these records is in the public interest because it will significantly contribute to public understanding of local law enforcement operations, accountability mechanisms, and community relations.If this request is denied in whole or in part, please justify all deletions or redactions by reference to specific exemptions in the public records law. If portions of these records are exempt, please redact the exempt portions and release the remainder of the records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Tristann Harrison

RE: FOIL Records Request of November 30, 2025, Reference # R018655-113025 
Dear EJ Fox, 
The New York State Police received a FOIL request from you on November 30, 2025. 
In accordance with your request, a copy of the Incident Report (which contains toxicology information), Accident Report, Reconstruction Report and photographs located responsive to your request is available to you through your GOVQA portal account.  You may access your record here through the FOIL Records Access Center and then selecting My Records Center. 
When applicable, redactions or exemptions have been made: 
- to identifying information such as addresses, dates of birth and telephone numbers to prevent an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy (Public Officers Law § 87(2)(b)). 
- to those portions which were compiled for law enforcement purposes and which, if disclosed, would identify a confidential source or disclose confidential information relating to a criminal investigation and/or would endanger the lives or safety of [others or the public or our members] (Public Officers Law § 87(2)(e)(iii) and Public Officers Law § 87(2)(f)). 
- of autopsy records which are exempt pursuant to County Law §677(3)(b). 
- of death certificate records which are exempt pursuant to Public Health Law § 4174. 
- of 911 records are exempt from disclosure by state statute, specifically County Law § 308(d). 
Please be advised that additional time is required to appropriately complete the body worn camera (“BWC”) portion of your request. A determination as to the grant or denial of your request will be made by or before April 30, 2027. 

This extension is necessary due to the high volume of all record requests currently being processed by this agency. Additionally, the volume of BWC footage maintained by this agency may require time-consuming searches and retrieval efforts. Considering the records maintained by this law enforcement agency are generally sensitive in nature, thorough review of any responsive BWC is necessary to prevent the disclosure of confidential and/or sensitive information. An additional factor towards the length of this extension is that the BWC redaction process is distinctively more time consuming due to its complexity and technology resources necessary to make applicable redactions.  Finally, this agency processes requests in the order they are received and requests that are particularly voluminous or complex may require additional time to complete. 
A search of our files failed to locate any records responsive to your request as it relates to internal review/investigation documents and any records we may have had concerning NYSP communications have met our criteria for purging and therefore have been destroyed. You may wish to contact Dutchess County 911 for records concerning the above. 
Due to the volume of requests received by this agency and the resulting delay in our response, the statutory fee ordinarily charged in FOIL requests such as yours is being waived. 
Pursuant to Public Officers Law § 89(4)(a), any person denied access to a record may appeal such determination in writing or through the FOIL Records Access Center within thirty (30) days.  If mailing, please state a specific ground for the appeal and send to: 
New York State Police FOIL Appeals Officer 
1220 Washington Avenue, Bldg. 22 
Albany, NY 12226-2252 
For more information on the FOIL Appeals process, please visit this FAQ. 
Sincerely, 
New York State Police 
1220 Washington Avenue, Bldg. 22 
Albany, NY 12226-2252

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Attleboro Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Attleboro Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

title: FBI: Joseph Ogden Dowdy

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FBI: Joseph Ogden Dowdy
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any bureau documents related to Joseph Ogden Dowdy. Dowdy (born September 24th 1949 in Hudson, Colorado - died January 17th 2008 in Salt Lake City, Utah) had an extensive criminal record. Dowdy was found guilty in federal court of the "illegal transportation of wildlife in interstate commerce" and was sentenced to time in federal prison. 

A copy of his obituary should be attached to this request and another can be found here: https://www.serenicare.com/obituaries/joseph-dowdy

DOWDY's extensive criminal record has been discussed in blog posts online: https://lostnfoundblogs.com/f/paul-hibbard-the-marvins---absent-anonymous

This is a request for records about JOSEPH OGDEN DOWDY from any and all FBI offices, including HQ, field offices, legal attaches, and facilities that maintain records under the FBI’s control. Please conduct a search for any records on DOWDY held by the Salt Lake City, Denver, Cheyenne, Casper, Lander or Albuquerque field offices. DOWDY was a long time resident of both New Mexico and Wyoming. According to a blog post I just read, it is important that I state the following: "As you know, your agency is required to search the records stored at NARA’s Washington Records Center in Suitland, MD, but still technically under your agency’s control. For more information see 36 CFR 1250.8" Please also conduct a physical search of records at NARA's Washington Records Center in Suitland, for any records or documents related to JOSEPH OGDEN DOWDY. 

Please include all potentially responsive materials, including but not limited to all communications, reports, inquiries, investigations, photographs, audio files, video files, memos, directives, etc. Please include all materials found in other subject files and all materials associated with any potentially-related names and any other known aliases, nicknames, code names, or any other identifying pseudonyms or references utilized by this agency. Please consult the Central Records System and records, the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Data Management System and records, Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) records, Physical Surveillance (FISUR) records, Technical Surveillance (TESUR) records, and all available cross-reference indices, databases, and records, in addition to any other locations containing potentially-responsive materials related to JOSEPH OGDEN DOWDY.

If the bureau cannot fulfill certain parts of this request or certain portions must be redacted please provide any reasonable segregable portion of a requested record after removing or redacting those portions claimed to be exempt, explain in writing the justification for redacting the record, indicate the extent of any redactions on the portion of the record which is made available or published and where technically feasible indicate on the redacted portion itself the specific exemption(s) claimed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

As posted on the Montana Board of Pardons and Parole Website at the following location: https://bopp.mt.gov/Feedback

The Montana Constitution (Art. II, sec. 9<https://leg.mt.gov/bills/mca/title_0000/article_0020/part_0010/section_0090/0000-0020-0010-0090.html>) affords the public the right to examine documents of all public bodies or agencies of the State of Montana. These requests are also known as “right to know,” “public information,” “public record,” “PIR,” but not FOIA. Freedom of Information Act is a federal right-to-know law that does not apply or control the retention or release of state records.

title: Jail Booking Log / Arrest Register (Jan 2025-Present)

communications.subject: North Carolina Public Records Law Request: Jail Booking Log / Arrest Register (Jan 2025-Present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

To the Custodian of Records, Wake County Sheriff's Office:

Under the North Carolina Public Records Act, N.C.G.S. Section 132-1 et seq., I request the following existing records, in the public interest and not for any commercial purpose.

I request the facility's daily jail booking log (booking register / arrest blotter) for every individual booked into the Wake County Detention Center from January 1, 2025 to the present. For each booking, I request the existing fields your jail-management system already records:

1. Booking or system number;
2. Name;
3. Date and time of booking;
4. Date of release;
5. The charge(s) or hold(s) associated with the booking, as recorded in the charges field;
6. Arresting or committing agency;
7. Warrant or reference number.

This is the facility's routine booking log -- ordinary public booking information -- and I request it in the existing electronic format your jail-management system exports (a spreadsheet, CSV, or delimited file is preferred; I do not require a formatted report). N.C.G.S. Section 132-6.2 provides that public records maintained in electronic form shall be made available in electronic form. Producing an export or query of data already maintained in your system is retrieval of an existing record, not the creation of a new one.

This request is not a duplicate of Records Request No. 26-3175, which concerned a narrower subject and was closed without production of any booking log; this request seeks the Office's general booking log for all bookings in the period, a different and broader record. The booking log is the Office's own jail record and the Office is its custodian. N.C.G.S. Section 132-6.2 provides that public records maintained in electronic form shall be made available in that form, and an agency may not decline to produce them because responding requires retrieving data from a database. I am requesting the existing booking data for all bookings in the period, in any export format your system supports.

As a public-interest, non-commercial request, I ask for a fee waiver or reduction; if a fee applies, please provide an itemized written estimate before incurring any cost, and I will respond promptly, including by narrowing the date range if that helps. If any portion is withheld, please state in writing the specific legal basis as N.C.G.S. Section 132-6(a) requires, and please preserve all responsive records pending resolution. Thank you.

Glen Wasserstein
(929) 786-1863

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Glen Wasserstein

title: LexisNexis Community Crime Map Contributors - Initial Sweep

communications.subject: Government Records Access and Management Act Request: LexisNexis Community Crime Map Contributors - Initial Sweep
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Government Records Access and Management Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request is related to the Community Crime Map (CCM) and Accurint, both are products of LexisNexis. You are receiving this request because your agency has data at communitycrimemap.com. We are seeking documents about how your agency integrates with LexisNexis, and whether your agency shares RMS/CAD/JMS data with other law enforcement agencies via Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) or Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx). 

We are requesting:
1) Technical integration documents: Any documents, integrations instructions, tutorials, and similar documents from LexisNexis about how to connect your RMS/CAD/JMS systems to LexisNexis's systems. [Typically held by IT or records systems teams/vendors from when your agency originally integrated with LexisNexis's systems]
2) Agreements: The signed "XML Addendum", Database Interface Agreement, or similar legal agreement that dictates how your agency's data may be used and shared. [Typically held by legal or procurement departments]
3) Shared Data: An export of what data you share with CCM and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with (CCM only, or also other law enforcement agencies?) [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]

Finally, are you able to tell me whether your law enforcement data sharing is restricted to a local consortium of agencies, or if it's shared generally with other law enforcement agencies within the LexisNexis portal?

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

Hi Derrek,

I understand you'd like to charge $812 for 14 hours of work. Based on how other agencies have handled the same request, and the instructions I provided, this should take significantly less time, likely under an hour.

I'd like to narrow it to an hour or less. To that end:

2) For the procurement record, I'm requesting a single document that should be quick to retrieve. LexisNexis uses nearly the same template across its customers, so here's an example to aid your search: https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/28549832-san-luis-obispo-avcc-addendum/

I'm hoping this compromise saves you time while providing transparency to the public.

If you believe the simplified request will take more than an hour, please confirm that the lowest-paid employee qualified to do the work earns $58 an hour, and provide an itemized breakdown showing each task performed, who performed it, their hourly rate, and the time spent on each. I'll also note that under Utah Code § 63G-2-203, and as the court held in Graham v. Davis County (1999 UT App 136), an agency may not charge for merely assembling documents. None of the records I'm requesting contain sensitive law enforcement information or PII, and not one of the dozens of agencies that have already produced them to me found any reason to redact them.

I'd like to resolve this directly and without creating an undue burden on your agency, while ensuring the public understands how your agency shares local police records with LexisNexis.

Thank you,
Shawn
